title: What Do Digital Traces Predict? Task Effects, Student Differences, and Critical Online Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2611.20803v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Digital assessment traces are increasingly used to predict student performance, often evaluated by correlating predicted and observed scores pooled across tasks. However, such correlations may reflect between-task differences rather than performance differences among students within tasks. To investigate this, we analyzed up to 527 browsing sessions from 424 university students completing open-Internet Critical Online Reasoning tasks and assessed the cross-task stability of their ratings. We evaluated the same out-of-fold predictions within and across tasks, compared three validation tiers up to leave-one-task-out, and tested incremental predictive contributions of consultation order and relational structure against matched permutation and randomization controls. None of the twelve prespecified primary tests was significant: on held-out tasks, consulted-page features showed no significant association with relative student performance, no

translated_title: 数字痕迹能预测什么？任务效应、学生差异与批判性在线推理
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.20803v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：数字评估痕迹正日益被用于预测学生表现，其有效性通常通过将所有任务汇总后的预测分数与观测分数之间的相关性来评估。然而，这种相关性可能反映的是任务之间的差异，而非任务内部学生之间的表现差异。为探究这一问题，我们分析了424名大学生完成开放互联网批判性在线推理任务的最多527个浏览会话，并评估了评分的跨任务稳定性。我们在任务内与跨任务间评估了相同的折外预测，比较了直至留一任务法的三种验证层级，并在匹配的置换检验和随机化对照条件下，检验了网页浏览顺序与关系结构特征的增量预测贡献。结果发现，十二项预先设定的主要检验中没有任何一项显著：在保留任务上，所浏览页面的特征与学生的相对表现之间不存在显著关联……
tldr: 该研究通过对批判性在线推理任务浏览数据的严格跨任务验证发现，数字痕迹特征无法显著预测任务内学生的相对表现差异，提示以往报告的预测相关性可能主要源于任务间差异而非学生个体差异。
en_tdlr: This study shows that, under strict cross-task validation on Critical Online Reasoning tasks, digital trace features show no significant association with relative student performance, suggesting previously reported predictive correlations may largely reflect between-task differences rather than genuine student differences.
